q: Which statement about black-box test techniques is correct?
o: Test cases are independent of how the software is implemented, so they remain useful if the implementation changes but the required behavior stays the same
Test cases can only be created after the code is written
Test cases are based on the internal structure of the test object
Their effectiveness depends mainly on the tester's experience
e: Las técnicas de caja negra (basadas en la especificación) analizan el comportamiento especificado sin mirar la estructura interna; por eso sus casos siguen valiendo si cambia la implementación.

q: Why can white-box test cases only be created after the design or implementation of the test object?
o: Because they depend on how the software is designed, i.e., on its internal structure and processing
Because they are derived from user stories
e: Las técnicas de caja blanca (basadas en la estructura) analizan la estructura interna, así que necesitan el diseño o la implementación.

q: Which statement about experience-based test techniques is correct?
o: They can detect defects that may be missed by black-box and white-box techniques, so they are complementary to them
They replace black-box and white-box techniques
Their effectiveness does not depend on the tester's skills
They are based on the analysis of the code structure
e: Las técnicas basadas en la experiencia aprovechan el conocimiento del tester; su eficacia depende mucho de sus habilidades y complementan a las de caja negra y blanca.

q: Black-box test techniques are also known as:
e: Caja negra = basadas en la especificación; caja blanca = basadas en la estructura.

q: White-box test techniques are also known as:
e: Las técnicas de caja blanca también se llaman basadas en la estructura.

q: In which test activities do test techniques support the tester?
o: Test analysis (what to test) and test design (how to test)
e: Las técnicas apoyan el análisis (qué probar) y el diseño (cómo probar): ayudan a definir condiciones, identificar elementos de cobertura y datos de prueba.

q: Which technique category is being used when a tester derives test cases by analysing the branches of the source code?
e: Analizar las ramas del código es una técnica de caja blanca (prueba de ramas).

q: Which technique category is being used when a tester derives test cases from equivalence partitions defined in the requirements?
e: La partición de equivalencia aplicada a requisitos especificados es una técnica de caja negra.

q: Which technique category is being used when a tester anticipates defects based on failures seen in similar applications?
e: Anticipar defectos a partir de la experiencia (error guessing) es una técnica basada en la experiencia.

q: What is the main purpose of using test techniques?
o: To develop a relatively small, but sufficient, set of test cases in a systematic way
To guarantee that all defects are found
e: Las técnicas ayudan a obtener de forma sistemática un conjunto de casos relativamente pequeño pero suficiente.

q: In statement testing, what are the coverage items?
e: En la prueba de sentencias los elementos de cobertura son las sentencias ejecutables.

q: How is statement coverage measured?
o: Number of statements exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of executable statements, as a percentage
Number of branches exercised divided by the total number of branches
Number of test cases passed divided by the number of test cases run
Number of lines of code divided by the number of test cases
e: Cobertura de sentencias = sentencias ejercitadas / sentencias ejecutables totales, en porcentaje.

q: Which statement about 100% statement coverage is correct?
o: It ensures every executable statement has been exercised at least once, but it may not detect data-dependent defects such as division by zero
It guarantees that all branches have been exercised
It guarantees that the code is defect-free
It ensures that all paths through the code have been tested
e: El 100 % de sentencias garantiza ejecutar cada sentencia, pero no detecta todos los defectos (p. ej., dependientes de datos) ni garantiza ejercitar todas las ramas.

q: Why might 100% statement coverage NOT ensure that all the decision logic has been tested?
o: Because it may not exercise all the branches in the code, e.g., the false outcome of an IF without ELSE
Because statement coverage counts only comments
Because statement coverage requires every path to be executed
Because statement coverage is a black-box measure
e: Un IF sin ELSE puede cubrirse con la salida verdadera ejecutando todas las sentencias, sin probar nunca la salida falsa.

q: Consider the code below. What is the minimum number of test cases needed to achieve 100% statement coverage?
e: Un único test con a = 11 y b = 6 ejecuta todas las sentencias (las dos condiciones son verdaderas). La cobertura de sentencias no exige probar las salidas falsas.
code:
IF a > 10 THEN
    x = 1
ENDIF
IF b > 5 THEN
    y = 2
ENDIF

q: What is the main benefit of achieving 100% statement coverage?
o: Each statement containing a defect will be executed, which may cause a failure that demonstrates the defect
All requirements are guaranteed to be implemented
All combinations of inputs have been tested
No regression testing is needed afterwards
e: El syllabus indica que, con el 100 %, cada sentencia con un defecto se ejecuta, lo que puede provocar un fallo que demuestre su presencia.

q: A program has 40 executable statements. The tests exercise 30 of them. What is the statement coverage?
e: Cobertura = 30 / 40 = 75 %.

q: Which statement about statement coverage and branch coverage is correct?
o: Branch coverage subsumes statement coverage: 100% branch coverage achieves 100% statement coverage, but not vice versa
Both always require the same number of test cases
Branch coverage is a black-box coverage measure
e: Cualquier conjunto que logre el 100 % de ramas logra el 100 % de sentencias, pero no al revés.

q: What is a branch, according to the syllabus?
o: A transfer of control between two nodes in the control flow graph, either unconditional or conditional
A path from the start to the end of the program
A combination of conditions in a decision table
e: Una rama es una transferencia de control entre dos nodos del grafo de flujo de control; puede ser incondicional (código lineal) o condicional (resultado de una decisión).

q: For the code below, what is the minimum number of test cases needed to achieve 100% branch coverage?
e: Hay que recorrer las salidas verdadera y falsa de las dos decisiones. Un test con ambas verdaderas y otro con ambas falsas lo consiguen: 2 tests.
code:
IF a > 10 THEN
    x = 1
ENDIF
IF b > 5 THEN
    y = 2
ENDIF

q: Which of the following corresponds to conditional branches?
o: The outcomes of an IF decision, the outcomes of a switch/case statement, and the decision to exit or continue a loop
Only the lines of code inside a function
Only the comments in the code
e: Las ramas condicionales corresponden a los resultados verdadero/falso de un IF, a las salidas de un switch/case o a la decisión de salir o continuar un bucle.

q: Which defect might NOT be detected even with 100% branch coverage?
o: A defect that requires the execution of a specific path through the code
A defect in a statement that is never executed
A defect in the false outcome of an IF decision
A defect in the default case of a switch statement
e: Ejercitar todas las ramas no garantiza detectar defectos que solo aparecen al recorrer un camino concreto.

q: In branch testing, how is coverage measured?
o: Number of branches exercised by the test cases divided by the total number of branches, as a percentage
Number of decisions divided by the number of statements
Number of paths divided by the number of branches
Number of failed tests divided by the number of branches
e: Cobertura de ramas = ramas ejercitadas / total de ramas, en porcentaje.

q: For the code below, which set of tests achieves 100% branch coverage with the minimum number of tests?
e: Hacen falta las dos salidas de la decisión: x > 0 (p. ej., 5) y x ≤ 0 (p. ej., -5). Un solo valor cubre solo una rama, y 5, 6 y 7 recorren todos la misma.
code:
IF x > 0 THEN
    PRINT "positive"
ELSE
    PRINT "not positive"
ENDIF

q: What is a fundamental strength shared by all white-box test techniques?
o: The entire software implementation is taken into account, which helps detect defects even when the specification is vague, outdated or incomplete
They can detect missing requirements (defects of omission)
They can be applied before any design exists
They do not require any knowledge of the code
e: La fortaleza de la caja blanca es considerar toda la implementación, útil aunque la especificación sea vaga, obsoleta o incompleta.

q: What is a corresponding weakness of white-box testing?
o: If the software does not implement one or more requirements, white-box testing may not detect the resulting defects of omission
It cannot be used to measure code coverage
It cannot be applied at component level
It always requires an independent test team
e: Si un requisito no se implementó, no hay código que cubrir, así que la caja blanca puede no detectar ese defecto de omisión.

q: How can white-box test techniques be used in static testing?
o: For example, during dry runs of code, or reviewing code not yet ready for execution and pseudocode
They cannot be used in static testing
e: Las técnicas de caja blanca sirven en prueba estática: dry runs de código, revisión de código aún no ejecutable, pseudocódigo y lógica modelable con un grafo de flujo.

q: Why is performing only black-box testing considered insufficient for measuring code coverage?
o: Black-box testing does not provide a measure of actual code coverage
Black-box testing cannot find any defects
Black-box testing always achieves 100% code coverage
Black-box testing is only allowed at acceptance level
e: Solo con caja negra no se mide la cobertura real del código; la caja blanca da una medida objetiva y permite generar pruebas adicionales.

q: How do white-box coverage measures help increase confidence in the code?
o: They provide an objective measurement and the information needed to generate additional tests to increase coverage
They replace the need for black-box testing
They prove that the code has no defects
They reduce the number of requirements
e: Las métricas de cobertura de caja blanca dan una medida objetiva y la información para crear tests adicionales, lo que aumenta la confianza en el código.

q: Which of the following can be modelled with a control flow graph and is therefore suitable for white-box techniques in reviews?
o: Pseudocode and other high-level or top-down logic
e: El syllabus indica que la caja blanca encaja en revisiones de pseudocódigo y otra lógica de alto nivel modelable con un grafo de flujo de control.

q: Which coverage-related white-box techniques are mentioned in the syllabus as being outside its scope?
o: More rigorous techniques used in safety-critical environments and coverage not related to code, such as neuron coverage
e: El syllabus solo trata prueba de sentencias y de ramas; menciona como fuera de alcance técnicas más rigurosas (entornos críticos), las de niveles superiores (API) y coberturas no basadas en código (cobertura de neuronas).

q: Which test technique uses the tester's knowledge of past failures and typical developer mistakes to anticipate errors, defects and failures?
e: El error guessing anticipa errores, defectos y fallos basándose en el conocimiento del tester: cómo funcionó la aplicación, errores típicos de los desarrolladores y fallos en aplicaciones similares.

q: What are fault attacks?
o: A methodical way to implement error guessing, using a list of possible errors, defects and failures to design tests that expose them
Security penetration tests performed by external hackers
e: Los fault attacks son una forma de implementar el error guessing: se crea o adquiere una lista de posibles errores, defectos y fallos y se diseñan tests para provocarlos o exponerlos.

q: Which of the following is a source of knowledge for error guessing mentioned in the syllabus?
o: The types of failures that have occurred in other, similar applications
The number of user stories in the backlog
e: Fuentes: cómo funcionó la aplicación en el pasado, los errores típicos de los desarrolladores y los fallos en aplicaciones similares.

q: A tester tests an input field with an empty value, a very long string and special characters, because such inputs often caused failures in the past. Which technique is this?
e: Elegir entradas porque históricamente causan fallos es error guessing (relacionado con errores de entrada).

q: Error guessing considers errors related to which areas, according to the syllabus?
o: Input, output, logic, computation, interfaces and data
e: El syllabus enumera: entrada, salida, lógica, cálculo, interfaces y datos.

q: How can the lists used in fault attacks be built?
o: From experience, defect and failure data, or common knowledge about why software fails
Only from the code coverage report
e: Las listas pueden basarse en la experiencia, en datos de defectos y fallos o en el conocimiento común de por qué falla el software.

q: "Wrong operator" and "missing cases" are examples of errors related to which category used in error guessing?
e: El syllabus da "missing cases, wrong operator" como ejemplos de errores de lógica.

q: In which situation is exploratory testing most useful?
o: When specifications are few or inadequate, or there is significant time pressure on testing
When exact, repeatable regression scripts are required
When 100% statement coverage must be demonstrated
When the tester has no domain knowledge
e: La prueba exploratoria es útil con especificaciones escasas o pobres, con mucha presión de tiempo y para complementar técnicas más formales. Es más eficaz con testers experimentados.

q: What characterizes exploratory testing?
o: Tests are simultaneously designed, executed and evaluated while the tester learns about the test object
Tests are fully scripted before execution
Tests are derived only from the source code
Tests are executed only by automation tools
e: En la prueba exploratoria se diseñan, ejecutan y evalúan pruebas a la vez mientras se aprende sobre el objeto.

q: In session-based exploratory testing, what guides the tester during the time-boxed session?
o: A test charter containing test objectives
e: En el enfoque basado en sesiones se trabaja en un timebox guiado por un test charter con objetivos; después suele haber un debriefing.

q: What usually follows an exploratory test session in session-based testing?
o: A debriefing involving a discussion between the tester and stakeholders interested in the results
A formal inspection of the code
e: Tras la sesión suele haber un debriefing con los stakeholders interesados en los resultados.

q: Which statement about exploratory testing is correct?
o: It can incorporate the use of other test techniques, such as equivalence partitioning
It cannot be combined with other techniques
It does not involve any coverage items
e: La prueba exploratoria puede incorporar otras técnicas, como la partición de equivalencia. Los elementos de cobertura se identifican y ejercitan durante la sesión.

q: What can testers use to document the steps followed and the discoveries made during exploratory testing?
e: El tester puede usar hojas de sesión (test session sheets) para documentar los pasos y los hallazgos.

q: Exploratory testing will be more effective if the tester:
o: Is experienced, has domain knowledge and has a high degree of essential skills like curiosity and creativeness
Has never seen the application before and has no domain knowledge
Follows a fixed script without deviation
e: El syllabus indica que la prueba exploratoria es más eficaz con testers experimentados, con conocimiento del dominio y con habilidades analíticas, curiosidad y creatividad.

q: Which items should NOT be included in a checklist used for checklist-based testing?
o: Items that can be checked automatically, items better suited as entry or exit criteria, or items that are too general
Items that can be checked separately and directly
e: El syllabus dice que las listas de comprobación no deben incluir elementos comprobables automáticamente, ni otros más adecuados como criterios de entrada o salida, ni demasiado generales.

q: Why should checklists be regularly updated based on defect analysis?
o: Some entries become less effective as developers learn to avoid those errors, and new high-severity defects may need new entries
Because checklists must always grow in length
Because checklists are only valid for one test run
e: Algunas entradas pierden eficacia porque los desarrolladores aprenden a evitar esos errores, y hay que añadir otras por nuevos defectos graves, cuidando que la lista no se haga demasiado larga.

q: In the absence of detailed test cases, what can checklist-based testing provide?
o: Guidelines and some degree of consistency for the testing
Proof that the software is correct
e: Sin casos detallados, las listas de comprobación dan pautas y cierta consistencia. Si son de alto nivel habrá variabilidad: más cobertura potencial, pero menos repetibilidad.

q: What is the effect of using high-level checklists?
o: Some variability in the actual testing is likely, resulting in potentially greater coverage but less repeatability
e: Con listas de alto nivel, cada tester prueba de forma algo distinta: puede aumentar la cobertura, pero se reduce la repetibilidad.

q: How are checklist items often phrased?
o: In the form of a question that can be checked separately and directly
As detailed test procedures with expected results
e: Los elementos de una lista suelen formularse como preguntas, cada una comprobable por separado y directamente.

q: Which of the following is an example of a checklist supporting non-functional testing mentioned in the syllabus?
o: A state transition diagram for a login
e: El syllabus cita las 10 heurísticas de usabilidad (Nielsen) como ejemplo de lista de comprobación para prueba no funcional.

q: On which sources can checklists be built?
o: Experience, knowledge about what is important for the user, or an understanding of why and how software fails
e: Las listas pueden basarse en la experiencia, en lo que es importante para el usuario o en entender por qué y cómo falla el software.

q: What are the "3 C's" of a user story?
e: Card: el soporte que describe la historia. Conversation: cómo se usará el software. Confirmation: los criterios de aceptación.

q: What does the INVEST acronym describe?
o: Characteristics of good user stories: Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small and Testable
e: Las buenas historias de usuario cumplen INVEST: independientes, negociables, valiosas, estimables, pequeñas y comprobables.

q: Which three perspectives does collaborative user story writing take into account?
e: La colaboración permite una visión compartida de lo que hay que entregar desde tres perspectivas: negocio, desarrollo y testing.

q: If a stakeholder does not know how to test a user story, what may this indicate?
o: The story may not be clear enough, may not reflect something valuable to them, or they may just need help in testing
The story is ready for implementation
The story should be tested only by developers
e: El syllabus indica que puede significar que la historia no está clara, que no refleja algo valioso o que el stakeholder necesita ayuda para probar.

q: Which is the most common format for a user story?
o: As a [role], I want [goal to be accomplished], so that I can [resulting business value for the role]
e: Formato habitual: "As a [rol], I want [objetivo], so that I can [valor de negocio]", seguido de los criterios de aceptación.

q: Which techniques can be used for the collaborative authorship of user stories?
o: Boundary value analysis and decision tables
e: El syllabus menciona la lluvia de ideas y los mapas mentales.

q: "Given the user is logged in, When she adds an item to the cart, Then the cart shows 1 item." This acceptance criterion is written in which format?
e: Given/When/Then es el formato orientado a escenarios (BDD). El orientado a reglas usa listas de verificación o tablas de entrada-salida.

q: A list of bullet points such as "Password must have at least 8 characters" and "Password must contain a digit" is an example of:
e: Una lista de verificación con viñetas (o una tabla de entrada-salida) es el formato orientado a reglas.

q: Which of the following is a purpose of acceptance criteria?
o: To define the scope of the user story and reach consensus among stakeholders
To define the developer's coding standards
To list the defects found in production
e: Sirven para definir el alcance, lograr consenso, describir escenarios positivos y negativos, servir de base a la aceptación y permitir planificar y estimar con precisión.

q: Acceptance criteria are usually a result of which of the 3 C's?
e: El syllabus indica que los criterios de aceptación suelen resultar de la Conversation; los propios criterios son la Confirmation. "Commitment" y "Coverage" no forman parte de las 3 C.

q: From a testing perspective, acceptance criteria may be viewed as:
o: The test conditions that should be exercised by the tests
The exit criteria of the whole project
The defect reports of the user story
e: Los criterios de aceptación pueden verse como las condiciones de prueba que deben ejercitarse.

q: Can a team use a custom format for acceptance criteria instead of scenario-oriented or rule-oriented formats?
o: Yes, as long as the acceptance criteria are well-defined and unambiguous
No, only bullet point lists are allowed
Yes, but only if the product owner writes them alone
e: El syllabus permite un formato propio siempre que los criterios estén bien definidos y no sean ambiguos.

q: A parcel service charges by weight in whole kilograms: 1–5 kg standard rate, 6–20 kg medium rate, 21–30 kg heavy rate. Weights below 1 kg or above 30 kg are rejected. Using equivalence partitioning with both valid and invalid partitions, what is the minimum number of test values needed to achieve 100% equivalence partition coverage?
e: Particiones: invalid (too low), standard, medium, heavy, invalid (too high). Son 5 en total (incluidas las 2 inválidas) y basta un valor por partición: 5 valores.

q: A parcel service charges by weight in whole kilograms: 1–5 kg standard rate, 6–20 kg medium rate, 21–30 kg heavy rate. Weights below 1 kg or above 30 kg are rejected. Which set of weight values achieves 100% equivalence partition coverage (valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Hay 5 particiones (invalid (too low), standard, medium, heavy, invalid (too high)). Solo esta opción toca todas; las demás repiten una partición y se dejan otra sin cubrir.

q: A parcel service charges by weight in whole kilograms: 1–5 kg standard rate, 6–20 kg medium rate, 21–30 kg heavy rate. Weights below 1 kg or above 30 kg are rejected. The tests use the weight values 40, 19, 50. What equivalence partition coverage do they achieve (counting valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Los valores tocan 2 de las 5 particiones: cobertura = 2/5 = 40%. Dos valores de la misma partición cuentan una sola vez.

q: A cinema sets ticket prices by age in whole years: 0–12 child, 13–17 teen, 18–64 adult, 65–120 senior. Ages below 0 or above 120 are rejected as invalid. Using equivalence partitioning with both valid and invalid partitions, what is the minimum number of test values needed to achieve 100% equivalence partition coverage?
e: Particiones: invalid (too low), child, teen, adult, senior, invalid (too high). Son 6 en total (incluidas las 2 inválidas) y basta un valor por partición: 6 valores.

q: A cinema sets ticket prices by age in whole years: 0–12 child, 13–17 teen, 18–64 adult, 65–120 senior. Ages below 0 or above 120 are rejected as invalid. Which set of age values achieves 100% equivalence partition coverage (valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Hay 6 particiones (invalid (too low), child, teen, adult, senior, invalid (too high)). Solo esta opción toca todas; las demás repiten una partición y se dejan otra sin cubrir.

q: A cinema sets ticket prices by age in whole years: 0–12 child, 13–17 teen, 18–64 adult, 65–120 senior. Ages below 0 or above 120 are rejected as invalid. The tests use the age values 89, 11, 1. What equivalence partition coverage do they achieve (counting valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Los valores tocan 2 de las 6 particiones: cobertura = 2/6 = 33.3%. Dos valores de la misma partición cuentan una sola vez.

q: An exam grading module accepts integer scores from 0 to 100: 0–49 fail, 50–69 pass, 70–89 merit, 90–100 distinction. Scores outside 0–100 are rejected. Using equivalence partitioning with both valid and invalid partitions, what is the minimum number of test values needed to achieve 100% equivalence partition coverage?
e: Particiones: invalid (too low), fail, pass, merit, distinction, invalid (too high). Son 6 en total (incluidas las 2 inválidas) y basta un valor por partición: 6 valores.

q: An exam grading module accepts integer scores from 0 to 100: 0–49 fail, 50–69 pass, 70–89 merit, 90–100 distinction. Scores outside 0–100 are rejected. Which set of score values achieves 100% equivalence partition coverage (valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Hay 6 particiones (invalid (too low), fail, pass, merit, distinction, invalid (too high)). Solo esta opción toca todas; las demás repiten una partición y se dejan otra sin cubrir.

q: An exam grading module accepts integer scores from 0 to 100: 0–49 fail, 50–69 pass, 70–89 merit, 90–100 distinction. Scores outside 0–100 are rejected. The tests use the score values 98, 72, 27, 65, 29. What equivalence partition coverage do they achieve (counting valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Los valores tocan 4 de las 6 particiones: cobertura = 4/6 = 66.7%. Dos valores de la misma partición cuentan una sola vez.

q: A thermostat accepts integer set points from 10 to 30 °C. 10–17 °C activates eco mode, 18–24 °C comfort mode and 25–30 °C boost mode. Other values are rejected. Using equivalence partitioning with both valid and invalid partitions, what is the minimum number of test values needed to achieve 100% equivalence partition coverage?
e: Particiones: invalid (too low), eco, comfort, boost, invalid (too high). Son 5 en total (incluidas las 2 inválidas) y basta un valor por partición: 5 valores.

q: A thermostat accepts integer set points from 10 to 30 °C. 10–17 °C activates eco mode, 18–24 °C comfort mode and 25–30 °C boost mode. Other values are rejected. Which set of temperature values achieves 100% equivalence partition coverage (valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Hay 5 particiones (invalid (too low), eco, comfort, boost, invalid (too high)). Solo esta opción toca todas; las demás repiten una partición y se dejan otra sin cubrir.

q: A thermostat accepts integer set points from 10 to 30 °C. 10–17 °C activates eco mode, 18–24 °C comfort mode and 25–30 °C boost mode. Other values are rejected. The tests use the temperature values 20, 34, 4, 25, 24. What equivalence partition coverage do they achieve (counting valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Los valores tocan 4 de las 5 particiones: cobertura = 4/5 = 80%. Dos valores de la misma partición cuentan una sola vez.

q: A loan application accepts an integer loan term in months from 6 to 60: 6–12 short term, 13–36 medium term, 37–60 long term. Other terms are rejected. Using equivalence partitioning with both valid and invalid partitions, what is the minimum number of test values needed to achieve 100% equivalence partition coverage?
e: Particiones: invalid (too low), short, medium, long, invalid (too high). Son 5 en total (incluidas las 2 inválidas) y basta un valor por partición: 5 valores.

q: A loan application accepts an integer loan term in months from 6 to 60: 6–12 short term, 13–36 medium term, 37–60 long term. Other terms are rejected. Which set of term values achieves 100% equivalence partition coverage (valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Hay 5 particiones (invalid (too low), short, medium, long, invalid (too high)). Solo esta opción toca todas; las demás repiten una partición y se dejan otra sin cubrir.

q: A loan application accepts an integer loan term in months from 6 to 60: 6–12 short term, 13–36 medium term, 37–60 long term. Other terms are rejected. The tests use the term values 68, 8, 7. What equivalence partition coverage do they achieve (counting valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Los valores tocan 2 de las 5 particiones: cobertura = 2/5 = 40%. Dos valores de la misma partición cuentan una sola vez.

q: A password field accepts lengths from 8 to 64 characters. Lengths 8–11 are rated weak, 12–19 good and 20–64 strong. Shorter or longer passwords are rejected. Using equivalence partitioning with both valid and invalid partitions, what is the minimum number of test values needed to achieve 100% equivalence partition coverage?
e: Particiones: invalid (too low), weak, good, strong, invalid (too high). Son 5 en total (incluidas las 2 inválidas) y basta un valor por partición: 5 valores.

q: A password field accepts lengths from 8 to 64 characters. Lengths 8–11 are rated weak, 12–19 good and 20–64 strong. Shorter or longer passwords are rejected. Which set of length values achieves 100% equivalence partition coverage (valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Hay 5 particiones (invalid (too low), weak, good, strong, invalid (too high)). Solo esta opción toca todas; las demás repiten una partición y se dejan otra sin cubrir.

q: A password field accepts lengths from 8 to 64 characters. Lengths 8–11 are rated weak, 12–19 good and 20–64 strong. Shorter or longer passwords are rejected. The tests use the length values 43, 16, 80, 71. What equivalence partition coverage do they achieve (counting valid and invalid partitions)?
e: Los valores tocan 3 de las 5 particiones: cobertura = 3/5 = 60%. Dos valores de la misma partición cuentan una sola vez.

q: A shop gives a quantity discount for whole units ordered: 1–9 units no discount, 10–49 units 5%, 50–99 units 10%. Orders of 0 units or more than 99 units are rejected. Using equivalence partitioning with both valid and invalid partitions, what is the minimum number of test values needed to achieve 100% equivalence partition coverage?

q: Which statement about the state transition coverage criteria is correct?
o: Achieving 100% valid transitions coverage guarantees 100% all states coverage
Achieving 100% all states coverage guarantees 100% valid transitions coverage
All transitions coverage only exercises invalid transitions
Valid transitions coverage is weaker than all states coverage
e: Todos los estados es más débil que transiciones válidas; el 100 % de transiciones válidas garantiza el 100 % de estados, y todas las transiciones garantiza ambas.

o: To avoid defect masking, where one defect prevents the detection of another
Because invalid transitions cannot be automated
Because each invalid transition requires a new test environment
Because invalid transitions are not coverage items
e: Probar una sola transición inválida por caso evita el enmascaramiento de defectos.

o: Apply a valid code to a €50 cart; the total becomes €45
Apply an expired code; the message 'Code expired' appears and the total is unchanged
Apply 1,000 codes per second to measure response time
Check that the discount code field uses the corporate font
e: En ATDD se empieza normalmente por los casos positivos, después los negativos y finalmente los no funcionales.

q: In ATDD, what is the first step of the process?
o: A specification workshop where the user story and its acceptance criteria are analysed, discussed and written

q: User story: "As a registered user, I want to reset my password by email." Acceptance criteria: AC1 a reset link is sent to the registered email; AC2 the link expires after 30 minutes. Which test case is derived correctly using ATDD?
o: Given a registered user requests a reset, when 31 minutes pass and the link is used, then the system rejects the link as expired
Given any user, when they log in, then the dashboard loads in under 1 second
Given a registered user, when they change their profile picture, then it is saved
Given the database, when it is backed up, then the backup is encrypted
e: Los tests de ATDD se basan en los criterios de aceptación de la historia y no van más allá de ella. Este cubre AC2; las otras opciones prueban funcionalidades fuera de la historia.

q: Which statement about test cases created with ATDD is correct?
o: They must cover all the characteristics of the user story and should not go beyond the story
They should cover additional features not in the story to increase coverage
Two test cases should describe the same characteristic for redundancy
They must always be written in a programming language
e: Los tests deben cubrir todas las características de la historia sin ir más allá, y no debe haber dos tests que describan la misma característica.

q: In ATDD, after the positive test cases are done, what should the team do next?
e: Orden típico: casos positivos → casos negativos → características no funcionales (p. ej., eficiencia, usabilidad).

o: Team members with different perspectives, e.g., customers, developers and testers; or the tester individually after the workshop
Only an external test team after implementation

AC: JPG and PNG files up to 5 MB are accepted; other formats are rejected with 'Unsupported format'; larger files are rejected with 'File too large'. Which set of ATDD test cases covers all the acceptance criteria with no two tests describing the same characteristic?
o: Upload a 2 MB JPG (accepted); upload a 2 MB GIF (rejected: 'Unsupported format'); upload a 6 MB PNG (rejected: 'File too large')
Upload a 2 MB JPG (accepted); upload a 3 MB JPG (accepted); upload a 4 MB JPG (accepted)
Upload a 2 MB GIF (rejected); upload a 3 MB BMP (rejected)
Upload a 6 MB PNG (accepted); upload a 2 MB GIF (accepted)
e: Hace falta un caso por característica: formato aceptado, formato no soportado y tamaño excesivo. Repetir el mismo caso positivo no aporta, y la última opción contradice los criterios.
